points.text: Water reaching the measure of a kurr remains pure and is not rendered impure by anything falling into it, regardless of decomposition.
Water exceeding the measure of a rawiya is not rendered impure by decomposition unless an overpowering odor changes its smell.
If the characteristics of water such as taste, color, or smell change due to impurities, it becomes unsuitable for drinking and ablution.
The measure of two qullas is interpreted as equivalent to a kurr, reconciling narrations that cite two jars as the threshold for purity.
Water in a ghedir used for istinja or ghusl is subject to juristic disapproval (karaha) rather than absolute impurity, used only when necessary.
